= Test data

Sample files used by the tests, committed rather than generated at run time so a
test run writes nothing it does not own.

== `imdb/`

A miniature IMDb non-commercial export set in the published column layout:
`title.basics.tsv` (required), plus `title.akas.tsv`, `title.episode.tsv` and
`title.ratings.tsv` as the optional exports. `internal/imdb_datasets` imports
whatever is present, so this is enough to build a real offline index.

Two consumers:

* `cmd/tomovee`'s `load_datasets` test copies it into a temporary directory and
  lets the server build the index there.
* `internal/webui/e2e/run.mjs` copies it into the smoke fixture's datasets
  directory, so the binary under test builds its index at startup.

The titles are the real IMDb ids for The Matrix, The Matrix Reloaded, Breaking
Bad and The Shawshank Redemption. The end-to-end specs look The Matrix up by id,
so its id and release year are part of what they assert.

Both consumers copy rather than point at this directory, because the importer
writes its index database next to the exports and the repository must stay
clean.

== `media/`

Two one-frame MPEG-4 videos that `ffprobe` reads as real files, 706 bytes each.
They are named the way a user would name their files on purpose, because the
correction specs assert on how the scanner parses them: `Mystery.Film.2020.mkv`
and `Mystery.Film.2020.1080p.mkv` land in one catalog entry as two versions.

At 706 bytes they are far below the 50 MB `min_file_size_mb` default, which
would drop them before they ever reached the catalog, so the smoke fixture
config lowers that limit to 0.

Generated once with:

[source,sh]
----
ffmpeg -f lavfi -i color=c=black:s=64x64:r=5:d=1 -c:v mpeg4 -frames:v 1 out.mkv
----
